caption: the unknown is your friend.
author: richard sabiaga
transcript: Do you understand it now? You're not supposed to know how it happens. Your analytical mind could never comprehend the magic that the universe has in store for you. If you can predict how it happens, you're trying to create the future from the lens of the past, from evidence of how things have already gone. And if you're trying to use a past to predict a future, then wouldn't it make sense that you would only create the same predictable outcome? This scary unknown void that you're in, yeah buddy, that's the fucking point. You want magic in your life, but you're so focused on the comfort of familiarity that you're failing to see that the death of previous expectations is allowing you to choose a new life. So if you want your life to change, in the next three months do something new and be radically delusional. The unknown is your friend, and the sooner that you stop running is the sooner that your new life finds you.
title: Embrace the Unknown to Transform Your Life
one_liner: Clinging to the familiar keeps you stuck in predictable outcomes — the unknown is where real change begins.
key_points: Trying to predict the future using past evidence only recreates the same outcomes
Discomfort with the unknown is exactly where meaningful change happens
Letting go of old expectations opens the door to choosing a new life
Act: do something new in the next 3 months and be 'radically delusional' about what's possible
